chunks: Beware! Surely Allāh has provided for virtue those who are suited to it, for truth pillars (that support it), and for obedience protection (against deviation).

In every matter of obedience you will find Allāh's succour that will speak through tongues and accord firmness to hearts. It has sufficiency for those who seek sufficiency, and a cure for those who seek cure.
ai.seo_question: What is the divine succour provided for obedience in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) elucidates the metaphysical reality of divine assistance (ayn al-ta'ah) that accompanies obedience, a concept central to Shia understanding of spiritual sustenance. The text emphasizes that this support is not merely external but internal, manifesting as eloquence in speech and firmness in the heart, thereby providing sufficiency (kifayah) and healing (shifa) for the believer's needs. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that obedience is the conduit through which God's grace becomes tangible and stabilizing in the human soul.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Beware! Surely Allāh, the Glorified, has provided for virtue those who are suited to it, for truth pillars (that support it), and for obedience protection (against deviation).

In every matter of obedience you will find Allāh, the Glorified's succour that will speak through tongues and accord firmness to hearts. It has sufficiency for those who seek sufficiency, and a cure for those who seek cure.
